title: AI in construction: what are contractors actually using it for?
description: AI in construction for contractors with 40-500 staff: where it pays first, what your software already includes, the rules, and who signs off.
verdict: Contractors mostly use AI for office paperwork so far; almost none use it in field production.[^1][^2]
Your project software probably already ships AI features, so check your plan before buying anything new.[^3][^4]
AI drafts the request for information (RFI), log or submittal check; a licensed or accountable person reads and signs it.[^5][^6]
General chatbots misread contract clauses and cameras miss small safety gear, so start with narrow, checked jobs.[^7][^8]
Ask your broker whether the new Insurance Services Office (ISO) generative AI exclusions are on your liability policy.[^9][^10]

headings.rules: Which rules apply to AI at a construction company?

answers.human-role: Your people keep every sign-off: project managers approve AI drafts, engineers keep the seal, the competent person stops unsafe work, and estimators own the bid.[^11][^5][^6]
answers.ranked: AI pays first in project search, since staff lose about 5.5 hours a week looking for project data. RFI drafting and submittal checks come next.[^15][^19][^16]
answers.rules: Mostly rules you already follow: OSHA safety, engineering licensing, contract and insurance terms, and worker data and hiring laws. We found no OSHA standard written for AI.[^6][^5]
answers.what-goes-wrong: AI goes wrong most when nobody checks a confident answer, when pilots add steps crews skip, and when uploads or extra logins put drawings and systems at risk.[^7][^20][^49]
answers.something-else: Pick something else when your platform already has the feature, the job is quantity takeoff or vendor invoices, or the work is sealed design.[^3][^21] Dedicated takeoff and invoice tools fit those jobs better, and sealed design belongs to the engineer or architect of record.[^5][^13]

summary: AI for construction companies is software that reads and drafts the job's paperwork: RFIs, submittals, logs, minutes and spec searches.[^1] What changes: PMs review drafts instead of writing them, and search project files instead of hunting, which took 5.5 hours a week.[^11][^15] Licensed people still decide and sign.[^5][^6]
humanRole: Your team stays in charge of every sign-off: AI drafts, and the project manager, superintendent, engineer or estimator approves.[^11] Procore builds its agents to draft for a person to approve (vendor).[^11]

Licensed engineers keep judgement and the seal on delegated design; ASCE says AI cannot stand in for a professional engineer's (PE) judgement.[^5][^12] North Carolina's board says the licensee must be able to reproduce AI output independently.[^13]

Your competent person still stops the work: the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) defines that role as someone with authority to correct hazards promptly.[^6] A camera can flag a missing harness; only that person can act on it.
Estimators keep the bid number they sign. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) still projects about 17,600 estimator openings a year.[^14]

ranked.name: Project search pays first: answers from drawings, specs and files
ranked.why: AI pays first in project search, because staff lose about 5.5 hours a week looking for project data.[^15] Procore, Autodesk and Fieldwire now ship this search inside their platforms (vendor claims).[^16][^17][^18]
ranked.payoff: Minutes to answer a field question from the drawings and specs, sampled before and after.

ranked.name: Drafting and sorting requests for information (RFIs)
ranked.why: A 2013 study of 1,362 projects put each RFI at about 8 hours and $1,080 to process.[^19] AI can draft the question, but a person must shape each RFI, says AIA Contract Documents.[^20]
ranked.payoff: Hours from field issue to RFI sent, and the share sent back as unclear.

ranked.name: First-pass submittal checks against the spec
ranked.why: Procore and Buildertrend now sell submittal review features (vendor claims).[^16][^21]
ranked.payoff: Days from submittal received to first comments, counting misses found later.

ranked.name: Daily logs, meeting minutes and owner updates
ranked.why: AI drafts daily reports, client updates and meeting minutes for a person to review before sending. Raken and Buildertrend sell these features (vendor claims).[^22][^21]
ranked.payoff: Minutes per daily log or owner update, and the edits a superintendent makes before sending.

ranked.name: Estimating support: scope gaps and bid leveling
ranked.why: Among Associated General Contractors (AGC) survey respondents, 23% already use AI in estimating.[^1] Takeoff tools, their prices and their accuracy are in our estimating guide.
ranked.payoff: Scope gaps caught before bid day, and estimator hours per bid.

ranked.name: Contract and subcontract risk review
ranked.why: Procore sells a contract review agent; Trimble lists contract risk review as still in development (vendor claims).[^16][^23] A general chat model scored 0.33 accuracy on contract clauses in one study.[^7]
ranked.payoff: Risky clauses flagged per contract, checked against your project manager's own markup.

ranked.name: Back-office vendor invoice coding
ranked.why: Office and administrative work is the top AI use among AGC respondents, at 45%.[^1] Buildertrend sells AI bill capture (vendor claim).[^21]
ranked.payoff: Minutes per vendor invoice coded, and errors caught before payment.

ranked.name: Safety observations and protective gear flags: useful, but checked
ranked.why: Construction had 1,034 private-industry deaths in 2024, with falls a leading cause.[^24] Detection is uneven: one 2026 model scored below 0.40 on goggles and boots.[^8]
ranked.payoff: Hazards flagged and closed each week, with false alarms counted.

ownData.title: Which AI features already ship inside the contractor software you pay for?

Data-use terms differ most, from "never without permission" to anonymized training rights.[^18][^27]

tables.title: How accurate is AI on construction tasks?
tables.intro: AI is accurate on narrow tasks it was trained for, and weak as a general chatbot on contracts.[^7][^38] Safety cameras do well on helmets and vests, and worse on small gear and crowds.[^8][^39]

rules.name: OSHA competent person, 29 CFR 1926.32(f)
rules.what: The rules that apply are mostly ones you already follow: safety, licensing, insurance, contracts and worker data.[^6][^5] We found no OSHA standard written for AI. The competent person must still be someone with authority to correct hazards promptly.[^6]

rules.name: Engineering board guidance on AI (NCEES 6.10, North Carolina, North Dakota)
rules.what: If you self-perform engineering or delegated design, the licensee keeps responsible charge of AI output.[^13][^12] North Dakota added its own guidelines in November 2026.[^41]

rules.name: AIA contract terms on instruments of service
rules.status: Contract terms in force; guidance 29 Oct 2026
rules.what: Uploading an architect's drawings to a tool that trains on them may breach your license to use them.[^20] Check each tool's training terms first; our estimating guide covers the clause.

rules.name: ISO generative AI exclusions CG 40 47, CG 40 48 and CG 35 08
rules.status: Optional for insurers; filed in 49 states and DC
rules.what: Insurers can add these to your general liability policy to exclude claims tied to generative AI.[^9][^42] Insurance Business counted 2,369 filing records in force and no admitted replacement product.[^10] Check with your broker and counsel; not legal advice.

rules.name: Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act (BIPA)
rules.what: Face-match clock-in, such as Raken's AI Photo ID, scans face geometry, which BIPA treats as biometric data.[^22][^43] In Illinois you need written notice, a written release and a public retention policy first.[^43] Check with your broker and counsel; not legal advice.

rules.name: AI hiring rules: NYC Local Law 144 and Colorado SB 26-189
rules.status: NYC in force; Colorado from 1 Jan 2027
rules.what: If AI screens craft or office applicants, NYC requires a bias audit and 10 business days' notice.[^44] Colorado's law takes effect on 1 Jan 2027.[^45] AGC found 16% of contractors use AI in HR, recruiting or training.[^1]

rules.name: Proposed GSA clause GSAR 552.239-7001
rules.what: On General Services Administration (GSA) work, you would disclose when language models process government project data, and flow that duty down to subs.[^46]

watchOuts: AI goes wrong most when nobody checks a confident answer: general chatbots misread contract clauses and miss coordination problems.[^7] Have the project manager check every flag against the document itself.
Pilots fade when the tool adds steps. Pilot one job on one live project, count hours before and after, and drop any step crews skip.[^47]
Fake change-of-bank emails hit subs and suppliers; the FBI logged $3.05B in business email compromise losses in 2025.[^48] Never change bank details without a call-back to a known number.
Ransomware hit 131 construction firms in early 2026, up 44% on a year earlier.[^49] Each connected AI tool is one more login to lock down.
Uploading owner drawings to tools that train on them can breach the architect's license.[^20] Read the training terms first; Bluebeam's AI beta terms, for one, allow training on your files.[^30]

AI-written scope sheets sent to subs unedited. Keep a person editing anything that goes out, since AI output can't stand in for professional judgment, and keep juniors doing the work themselves.[^5][^20]

faq.q: How is AI used in construction?
faq.a: Mostly for office paperwork: 45% of AGC respondents use it there, and 23% in estimating.[^1] Field use is rare; a Census survey found 0.7% of construction firms using AI in production work.[^2]

faq.q: What is the best AI tool for a construction company?
faq.a: Usually the one already inside your project platform: Procore, Autodesk, Fieldwire and Bluebeam all ship AI features now.[^3][^17][^18][^25] Add a separate tool only for a job your platform can't do.

faq.q: Has any AI construction software survived a pilot?
faq.a: Not often: MIT research found most generative AI pilots show no profit-and-loss impact.[^47]
Yes, as a first pass against the spec, with a person signing off; Procore and Buildertrend sell this (vendor claims).[^16][^21]

faq.q: Is it safe to upload project documents to AI?
faq.a: Only to tools whose terms rule out training on your files, as Fieldwire's do without your permission.[^18] Raken keeps anonymized training rights, and owner drawings may carry license limits.[^27][^20]

faq.q: Will AI replace construction workers, project managers or estimators?
faq.a: No sign of it: BLS projects construction manager jobs to grow 9% from 2025 to 2035.[^50] AGC found 87% of firms with open craft jobs, and BLS counted 298,000 construction openings in September 2026.[^51][^52] Estimator jobs may dip 3%, yet about 17,600 open each year.[^14]

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy first: switch on what your project platform already includes, then add one narrow tool.[^3][^35] Most companies now buy AI: 76% of use cases, up from 53% in 2024.[^53]
buyVsBuild.build: Build only the glue that is your edge, such as your RFI template, spec library and approval step. MIT found bought or partnered tools succeed about 67% of the time; internal builds about a third as often.[^47]

pickElse: Pick something else when your platform already has the feature: turn on Procore's agents, Autodesk Assistant or Fieldwire Field Intelligence first.[^3][^17][^18]
The job is quantity takeoff: use a dedicated takeoff tool from our estimating guide. General chat models test weak even on construction contract questions.[^7][^38]
The work is sealed design: the engineer or architect of record owns it, not the contractor's AI.[^5][^13]
The job is vendor invoices: an accounts-payable capture tool, such as Buildertrend Bill Capture, fits better; see our invoice guide.[^21]

offer.heading: Which paperwork job should your PMs hand AI first?
offer.body: Hand AI project search first, then RFI drafting, since staff lose about 5.5 hours a week hunting for project data. In a free 30-minute call we map one job on one live project, such as RFIs or daily logs, against what your platform includes. You leave with a before-and-after measure and the point where your project manager or superintendent signs off.

reviews.notes: Dana (COO): the bottom line answers 'what are contractors using it for' and the human-role block names who signs (PM, super, engineer, estimator, competent person). Every ranked job has a payoff to measure. Problem: RFI, ISO, OSHA, AGC and GSA appeared before being spelled out. Fixed: each spelled out on first use (RFI and ISO in the bottom line, OSHA in the human-role block, AGC in the ranked list, GSA in the rules table). Every question heading now opens with a direct answer sentence; FAQ questions came from Reddit threads (r/ConstructionManagers, r/estimators, r/Construction), rival-page FAQ blocks and the keyword list.

Ops head: wants to know what changes on a live project and what to switch on. The own-data table answers what is already in Procore, Autodesk, Trimble, Bluebeam, Fieldwire, Buildertrend and Raken, with the admin control for Autodesk's training setting. Fixed: the back-office job promised payroll checks with no evidence, so it is now vendor invoice coding only; the pilot-fade watch-out now ends in a concrete control (one job, one live project, hours counted before and after). Payment-fraud watch-out keeps the call-back rule.

GM: wants to know what it costs and whether one project can try it. Costs on the page are external and dated: Bluebeam Max and Fieldwire Business tier prices read 26 Nov 2026, and 'Not published' where Procore, Autodesk, Trimble, Buildertrend and Raken give no AI price; no Zavient price, per site rules. Buy-or-build answers 'turn on what you already pay for first'. Fixed: the offer now says one job on one live project, and spells out project manager and superintendent instead of PM and super.

Head of estimating / project operations: wants evidence of accuracy and a clear line to the estimating page. The ranked estimating item links ai-construction-estimating, and its takeoff price table is not repeated here. The accuracy table gives the contract-clause and safety-camera results with their studies. Fixed: the RFI cost now says it is a 2013 study; the submittal FAQ now labels Procore and Buildertrend submittal review as vendor claims. Offer sentence trimmed to stay under 25 words.

Steve: the title and five bottom-line bullets answer the question in 10 seconds, and the own-data table tells him what his current software already includes. His worries are covered: data (each vendor's training terms), insurance (ISO exclusions, ask your broker), security (fake bank-change emails, ransomware), rules (engineer sign-off, BIPA, hiring laws). Gap he will notice: no case from a contractor his size, because none had a citable page; none is claimed. Fixed: the Census stat now names its secondhand sources in full instead of initials.

sources.name: Frontiers in Mechanical Engineering (2026), PPE attribution in crowds
sources.what: Matching PPE to the right worker falls from 97.1% to 84.6% as crowds grow.

sources.name: PLOS One (2025), progress tracking of window installation
sources.what: Detection score (mAP50) 0.953 on 768 images for window installation stages.

sources.name: North Dakota Board of Registration for Professional Engineers and Land Surveyors, Guidelines for AI usage (9 Nov 2026)
sources.what: State board guidance on engineers using AI.

sources.name: Big I (Independent Insurance Agents and Brokers of America), Verisk to roll out new GL exclusions for generative AI
sources.what: Trade-body summary of the ISO generative AI exclusions, 01 26 edition, optional for insurers.

sources.name: Illinois Biometric Information Privacy Act, 740 ILCS 14
sources.what: Face geometry scans are biometric identifiers; a private entity must inform the person in writing and get a written release before collecting them, and keep a public retention policy.

sources.name: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, Automated employment decision tools
sources.what: Local Law 144: bias audit, 10 business days' notice to candidates, penalties of $500 to $1,500.

sources.name: Colorado General Assembly, SB 26-189
sources.what: Signed 14 May 2026, replaces SB 24-205; effective 1 Jan 2027.

sources.name: Lathrop GPM, Your built environment project uses AI: does your risk allocation reflect that? (13 Oct 2026)
sources.what: GSA proposed GSAR 552.239-7001, requiring disclosure when language models process government project data, with flow-down to subcontractors; still proposed.

sources.name: Fortune, MIT report: 95% of generative AI pilots at companies failing (18 Aug 2025)
sources.what: MIT NANDA research: most generative AI pilots show no profit-and-loss impact; bought or partnered tools succeed about 67% of the time, internal builds about a third as often.

sources.name: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center, 2025 Internet Crime Report
sources.what: 24,768 business email compromise complaints and $3.05B in losses in 2025.

sources.name: GuidePoint Security, 5 industries most impacted by ransomware, Q1 2026
sources.what: 131 construction ransomware victims in Q1 2026, up 44% year on year; construction the fourth most-hit sector.

sources.name: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, Construction managers (27 Aug 2026)
sources.what: Projected +9% growth 2025-35, about 49,700 openings a year.

sources.name: AGC of America and NCCER, 2026 Workforce Survey (news release, 3 Sep 2026)
sources.what: 1,830 respondents, Jul-Aug 2026: 87% have openings for hourly craft positions and 82% for salaried positions; 73% expect to add employees.

sources.name: BLS, JOLTS Table 1, job openings by industry, seasonally adjusted (3 Nov 2026)
sources.what: Construction: 298,000 job openings in September 2026 (preliminary), up from 262,000 in August.

sources.name: Menlo Ventures, 2025 State of Generative AI in the Enterprise (9 Dec 2025)
sources.what: Survey of 495 US decision-makers: 76% of AI use cases bought rather than built, up from 53% in 2024.
